turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Howzit. Come through, I'll do your blood pressure before the doctor calls you. The computers have been slow all morning.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, thank you sister. Eish, I'm nervous hey. My hands keep going dead at night and I don't know if it's serious.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Shame. Arm straight for me. Right, that's a hundred and thirty eight over eighty six, and your pulse is seventy six.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): My own sister had numb fingers last year and she ended up with an operation on the wrist. She's fine, but that's her life, not yours.
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's been dropping cups at home. This morning she nearly smashed the mug I won at the braai.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, I did drop it. Things just slip. It happens at work too, the small parts.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): The doctor's battling with his screen. He'll be here now now. I'll leave you the file.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, sorry. It froze again. Ok. What brings you in today?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): My hands, doctor. At night they go numb, the thumb and the index and the middle finger, and I have to shake them to wake them up.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Say that again? I was still clicking.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Numb at night. Thumb, index, middle finger. Both hands, but the right is worse. I shake them until the feeling comes back.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): How long has this been happening?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, about three weeks, ag no, that's wrong. It's been closer to two months. I kept hoping it would pass.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm scared the factory will say I'm not coping. It's packaging work, the same movements all day, and some shifts are twelve hours.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mm. Is there pain, or only the numbness?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): There's an ache in the wrists as well, mostly at night. Not terrible. The right one is worse.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): Does the feeling run up the arm? Any pain in the neck?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing in the neck. It doesn't go up the arm, it stays in the hand. Sometimes those fingers tingle too.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): And in the daytime, numb then as well, or only at night?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly at night. Daytime they're alright unless I've been on the line for hours, then they tingle. Is that a stroke? My uncle had a stroke.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): I've been so worried I can't sleep properly. Do I need a scan? Am I going to lose the use of my hands? I have to work tomorrow.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hold on, err, blank screen again. You said a stroke?
[SEG0023] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Her uncle, her mother's brother, had a stroke at sixty. She's been on her phone half the night about it.
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): So is it a stroke, doctor? Please. Someone at work had a hand operation and she was off for ages. Is that where this is going?

[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): This pattern, the thumb and those two fingers, waking you and shaking the hand, that is the median nerve getting pinched in the carpal tunnel at the wrist. The tunnel gets tight and the nerve can't send proper signals, especially when the wrist is bent at night. It is not a stroke.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): So the nerve is squashed in the wrist? Will I need the operation? How long would I be booked off? Can I still do my shifts?

[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Not an operation today. What I want is a neutral wrist splint at night, so the wrist stays straight and that nerve isn't kinked. Wear it every night for the next few weeks.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh, a brace from the pharmacy? Do I wear it on the factory line? What if I can't fall asleep with it on? Will the numbness stop completely?
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Nights only, not on the line. Don't strap it so tight your fingers go blue. If it bugs you, loosen it, but try to keep it on.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tell him about the tablets, Thandi.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, ibuprofin, I mean ibuprofen. I thought the dose was four hundred milligrams, but no, the box is six hundred, twice a day, with food, for the ache.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): The dose again? I only half caught it.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Six hundred milligrams, not four hundred. Twice a day.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Six hundred twice a day. Any tummy trouble with it, ulcers, heartburn?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): No. My stomach is fine. No heartburn. Can I carry on with it together with the splint, or must I stop?
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Carry on with the ibuprofen for now if the stomach stays happy. Any allergies to medicines, or anything else?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): No, no allergies. Nothing. Could diabetes be doing this to the nerve? I don't think I have it. Do I need bloods?
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you already have diabetes, thyroid trouble, arthritis?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): No diabetes, no thyroid thing. I don't think it's arthritis. I had my gallbladder out about five years ago. Is that connected, sorry, I know that's a lot of questions.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Gallbladder's not connected, no. Do you smoke? What about drinking?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): I've never smoked. A glass of wine on a Friday, that's all, we're not big drinkers. If the splint doesn't fix it, then what happens?

[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the numbness hasn't settled once you've properly used the splint, we might send you for a nerve conduction test, to check how the median nerve is conducting. I'm not booking that test today.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Does that nerve test hurt, is it needles? Will medical aid cover it, and would I need a sick note to miss a shift? And when do I see you again?

[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Wires on the skin, mostly, more uncomfortable than sore. Come back and see me in six weeks so we can judge the splint. Reception will book it. If it gets properly worse before then, phone the rooms.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Ok. Splint from the pharmacy, nights only, back in six weeks. Thank you, doctor. Sorry I talked so much.
[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): Ag, you're fine. See you in six weeks.

spec.situation: Middle-aged office or factory worker with night-time numbness in thumb, index and middle fingers, shakes hands to wake them; dropping cups; splint advice, nerve test conditional.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: hedged_plan: the doctor hedges ('we might do a scan if it does not settle', 'let's see in two weeks'). Conditional vs planned status must follow the words.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Patient says stomach is fine; stomach pain was not specifically mentioned.

omissions.text: Daytime numbness is mostly absent; symptoms are mostly at night, with daytime tingling only after hours on the line.
Patient denied ulcers when specifically asked about 'tummy trouble with it, ulcers, heartburn'; only stomach trouble/heartburn were recorded, not ulcer history.
Doctor explicitly reassured that this is not a stroke.
Doctor said he is not booking the nerve conduction test today.
Nerve conduction test described as 'wires on the skin, mostly, more uncomfortable than sore.'
Wrist splint to be obtained from the pharmacy/a brace from the pharmacy was discussed and understood by the patient.
